chunks: O believers, do not ask about things which, if made known to you, may vex you. But if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed they will be unfolded to you. God has overlooked (your failings) in this (respect), for God is forgiving and forbearing.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'do not ask about things' in Surah Al-Ma'idah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the specific inquiry of the Companions regarding the 'Hudud' (fixed punishments) or the details of the Sabbath prohibition, illustrating the principle of *Takhfif* (easing of burdens) in Islamic jurisprudence. It underscores the divine wisdom of withholding exhaustive legal details until necessary, thereby preventing unnecessary hardship for the early Muslim community. The verse serves as a foundational text for understanding how divine forbearance (*Hilm*) balances strict legal revelation with practical mercy.
